Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=driver/main.cpp lines=33-47 kind=dead-code-block
Claim: kSubcommands reserves stub slots for 'profile', 'cluster', 'estimate' -- commands of the simpoint pipeline that was removed as a whole feature family and is planned in no ROADMAP.
Evidence given: Lines 44-47: `{"profile"}, {"cluster"}, {"estimate"}` routed to the 'not yet implemented' stub (main.cpp:211-222). Commit ff20602 'Remove icount trigger, simpoint-driven trigger, and cosim features' removed 'hsim profile/cluster/estimate' end to end; grep -in 'profile|estimate' over ROADMAP.md/ROADMAP_*.md finds no such feature. The comment (lines 33-37) claims they are 'stable slots for unfinished ROADMAP features', contradicted by the roadmaps. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh only asserts they never appear in help; no test exercises the rc-3 stub routing, so deleting the slots breaks nothing.

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Release-surface contract: the andesim PRODUCT help shows only the finished,
3	# user-facing commands (run, list, doctor) and never the third-party simulator
4	# name "verilator". The former developer commands build/test/state-diff have
5	# moved OUT of the binary (build -> scripts/build_all.sh, test ->
6	# scripts/test_all.sh, state-diff -> the diff_states core behind `run --verify`):
7	# they are not listed in any help and are not dispatchable. The unfinished
8	# ROADMAP commands (profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate) appear in no
9	# help at all. The cycle-accurate engine is presented as "vsim" everywhere --
10	# proven end to end with a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator" and
11	# must come back out as vsim:.
12	set -uo pipefail
13	
14	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
17	
18	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
19	
20	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
21	
22	# has RE TEXT  -- TEXT must match RE ; missing RE TEXT -- TEXT must NOT match RE
23	has()     { printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -Eq "$1"; }
24	no_word() { ! printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -qi 'verilator'; }
25	
26	# 1. release --help: a clear command TREE -- run/list/doctor are the major
27	# commands (column 0); each is followed by its indented subcommands (run's
28	# modes, list's targets); run carries its full option list with REQUIRED flags
29	# marked. No developer-commands section, no "verilator", no dev-only fixtures.
30	H=$("$BIN" --help 2>&1)
31	has '^run '    "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'run':"$'\n'"$H"
32	has '^list '   "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'list':"$'\n'"$H"
33	has '^doctor ' "$H" || fail "release --help: missing major command 'doctor':"$'\n'"$H"
34	for s in fast cycle hybrid; do
35	  has "^  $s " "$H" || fail "release --help: run missing subcommand '$s':"$'\n'"$H"
36	done
37	for t in models engines; do
38	  has "^  $t " "$H" || fail "release --help: list missing target '$t':"$'\n'"$H"
39	done
40	has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$H" || fail "release --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$H"
41	for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
42	  has "(^|  )$c " "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked non-release command '$c'"
43	done
44	no_word "$H" || fail "release --help: leaked 'verilator'"
45	has 'developer command' "$H" && fail "release --help: developer commands moved to scripts/; drop the section:"$'\n'"$H"
46	has '^  fixtures ' "$H" && fail "release --help: leaked dev-only 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$H"
47	ok "release --help: run/list/doctor tree with subcommands + REQUIRED flags, no dev/removed surface"
48	
49	# 2. The developer commands left the binary entirely: ANDESIM_DEV=1 --help adds
50	# NO commands (run/list/doctor only) -- it only reveals the dev 'fixtures'
51	# target. build/test/state-diff are not dispatchable.
52	D=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" --help 2>&1)
53	for c in run list doctor; do
54	  has "^$c " "$D" || fail "dev --help: missing major command '$c':"$'\n'"$D"
55	done
56	for c in build test state-diff profile cluster archive replay estimate; do
57	  has "(^|  )$c " "$D" && fail "dev --help: leaked removed/hidden command '$c'"
58	done
59	has '^  fixtures ' "$D" || fail "dev --help: should reveal the dev 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$D"
60	no_word "$D" || fail "dev --help: leaked 'verilator'"
61	for c in build test state-diff; do
62	  expect 2 "unknown command '$c'" "$BIN" "$c"
63	done
64	ok "dev --help: dev 'fixtures' target revealed, no developer commands; build/test/state-diff gone (rc 2)"
65	
66	# 3. run --help: the --engine example reads vsim:, never verilator:; the
67	# --trigger menu offers only the supported triggers (marker|pc).
68	RH=$("$BIN" run --help 2>&1)
69	has 'vsim:' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing vsim: example"
70	no_word "$RH" || fail "run --help: leaked 'verilator'"
71	has ' --mem-size' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --mem-size:"$'\n'"$RH"
72	has ' --mmap-size' "$RH" && fail "run --help: retired --mmap-size alias should stay hidden:"$'\n'"$RH"
73	# Interactive-debug + oracle knobs are user-facing: documented in the release help.
74	has '^  --verify '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --verify:"$'\n'"$RH"
75	has '^  --gdb '      "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb:"$'\n'"$RH"
76	has '^  --gdb-port ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --gdb-port:"$'\n'"$RH"
77	# run --help is sliced from the same tree: it shows the mode subcommands and
78	# marks the required flags (so a user sees --trigger is mandatory for hybrid).
79	has '^  fast '   "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'fast':"$'\n'"$RH"
80	has '^  hybrid ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing mode subcommand 'hybrid':"$'\n'"$RH"
81	has '^  --trigger ' "$RH" || fail "run --help: missing --trigger:"$'\n'"$RH"
82	has 'REQUIRED for hybrid' "$RH" || fail "run --help: --trigger not marked REQUIRED for hybrid:"$'\n'"$RH"
83	ok "run --help: vsim: example, modes + REQUIRED markers, no verilator, --mem-size/--verify/--gdb documented"
84	
85	# 4. list models: composition cells read vsim (never verilator), and NOTES show
86	# user-facing model traits only -- no implementation detail.
87	LM=$("$BIN" list models 2>&1)
88	has 'vsim' "$LM" || fail "list models: missing vsim"
89	no_word "$LM" || fail "list models: leaked 'verilator'"
90	for d in 'transparent passthrough' 'pure from reset'; do
91	  has "$d" "$LM" && fail "list models: leaked implementation detail '$d':"$'\n'"$LM"
92	done
93	ok "list models: vsim, no verilator, no implementation detail"
94	
95	# 5. list engines end to end: a fake engine that self-describes as "verilator"
96	# must surface as vsim: (the single normalization point), proving --engine /
97	# errors / list all speak the product name with no real sim_* needed.
98	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
99	cat >"$TMP/sim_fake" <<'EOF'
100	#!/bin/sh
101	[ "$1" = "--describe" ] && printf '%s\n' '{"id":"verilator:fakecfg","type":"verilator","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":256,"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
102	EOF
103	chmod +x "$TMP/sim_fake"
104	LE=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$TMP" "$BIN" list engines 2>&1)
105	has 'vsim:fakecfg' "$LE" || fail "list engines: fake not renamed to vsim:fakecfg:"$'\n'"$LE"
106	no_word "$LE" || fail "list engines: leaked 'verilator':"$'\n'"$LE"
107	# Triggers are a hybrid-MODEL option, not an engine attribute: `list engines`
108	# carries no TRIGGERS column.
109	has 'TRIGGERS' "$LE" && fail "list engines: TRIGGERS is a hybrid-model option, not an engine column:"$'\n'"$LE"
110	ok "list engines: a verilator-self-describing engine is shown as vsim:, no TRIGGERS column"
111	
112	# 6. `list fixtures` is a developer target (internal test ELFs, not user
113	# workloads): release list --help hides the target line; ANDESIM_DEV reveals
114	# it. (Checked as the '^  fixtures ' target line, not the bare word -- doctor's
115	# brief legitimately mentions checking fixtures are present.)
116	LH=$("$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
117	has '^  fixtures ' "$LH" && fail "release list --help: leaked 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
118	has '^  models '   "$LH" || fail "release list --help: missing 'models' target:"$'\n'"$LH"
119	expect 2 "unknown target 'fixtures'" "$BIN" list fixtures
120	DLH=$(ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list --help 2>&1)
121	has '^  fixtures ' "$DLH" || fail "dev list --help: missing 'fixtures' target:"$'\n'"$DLH"
122	ANDESIM_DEV=1 "$BIN" list fixtures >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "dev: list fixtures should succeed"
123	ok "list: fixtures is dev-only (release hides it; ANDESIM_DEV reveals it)"
124	
125	# 7. The removed `build` command must not survive in user-facing hints: a
126	# missing artifact in `doctor` now points at scripts/build_all.sh.
127	DOC=$(VSIM_BIN=/no/such/vsim "$BIN" doctor 2>&1 || true)
128	printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'andesim build' && fail "doctor hint still names the removed 'andesim build':"$'\n'"$DOC"
129	printf '%s\n' "$DOC" | grep -q 'scripts/build_all.sh' || fail "doctor hint should point at scripts/build_all.sh:"$'\n'"$DOC"
130	ok "doctor missing-artifact hint points at scripts/build_all.sh, not the removed command"
131	
132	ok "release surface (hide verilator + release/dev command split)"

commit ff2060273b07e0505e31fc06ec57691a8af01b48
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 26 15:00:02 2026 +0800

    Remove icount trigger, simpoint-driven trigger, and cosim features
    
    Removes three feature families end to end (code, build, tests, docs):
    
    - icount trigger: the --mode icount / --hybrid-icount / plugin icount=
      instruction-count drain path.
    - simpoint-driven trigger: the BBV profile -> SimPoint cluster -> per-phase
      drain pipeline (hsim profile/cluster/estimate, --mode simpoint), the
      plugin bbv_out=/slice=/slice_at=/drain_at_exit= modes, bbv_emit, and the

- Dependencies: F1, F2, F3
- TDD RED: `ctest -R rt_c_v_regs--orchestrator` is registered but the
  orchestrator's spawn path is incomplete; test fails. Then asserts
  exit-code parity with `rt_c_v_regs--csr` (the bash-harness version).

### F5 - icount counter + trigger in QEMU plugin

- Status: done. Trigger priority (spec section 5 row 1: CSR/PC > BBV >
  icount) is deferred - F5 registers icount tick FIRST in
  `vcpu_tb_trans`, so it wins on insns where both fire. The F5 e2e uses
  a CSR-less fixture, so this is invisible today; F11 (slice-consume)
  will revisit when BBV ties enter the picture.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: Add `uint64_t icount_retired` incremented in a per-insn
  callback registered alongside the CSR/PC matcher in
  `vcpu_tb_trans()`. New plugin arg `icount=N`. When
  `icount_retired >= icount_target`, set the should-exit flag and call
  `on_handoff` at the same insn boundary.
- Key files:
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:264-300` (`vcpu_tb_trans`)
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:302-339` (arg parser)
- Dependencies: F1
- TDD RED: `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_icount_trigger.sh` runs a fixture
  with `--plugin-args icount=100000` on a CSR-less binary; asserts the
  drained state file's `minstret >= 100000` and exit code is 200. Fails
  because the `icount=` arg is unknown.

### F6 - vsim IcountTrigger (sibling of CsrTrigger)

- Status: done. `HandoffController` was retrofitted to a class template
  on the trigger type (structural; CTAD preserves all existing call
  sites). `IcountTrigger` lives at `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp`
  with the duck-type surface (`lookup`, `empty`, `observe_commit`).
  `--hybrid-icount N` is wired in `main.cpp` and dispatches into
  `Simulator::enable_hybrid_icount_handoff`. Mutually exclusive with
  `--hybrid-exit-pc`. Unit test
  `tests/hybrid/icount_trigger.test.cpp` covers both the standalone
  trigger and the templated controller's drain.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: New `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` with the
  same duck-type surface as `CsrTrigger` (`lookup(pc) ->
  std::optional<hit>`, plus an `observe_commit()` that increments the
  per-hart counter). `HandoffController` is already template-parameterised
  on trigger type (`handoff_controller.hpp:38`). Add
  `--hybrid-icount N` to `main.cpp:466-472`. Multi-hart out of scope
  (plan-validation rejects `hart_id != 0`).
- Key files:
  - `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` (new)
  - `verilator/src/main.cpp:466-472`
  - `verilator/src/simulator.hpp:223-253` (registration)
- Dependencies: none (parallel to F5)
- TDD RED: `verilator/tests/hybrid/test_icount_trigger.cpp` (doctest)
  builds a `RecordingBus` + `IcountTrigger(N=100)`, drives 100 retire
  ticks, asserts `on_retire` returns a drained state at exactly the
  100th. Fails because the class does not exist.

### F7 - BBV emission plugin (profile mode)

- Status: done. `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.{c,h}` provides a self-contained
  SimPoint-format emitter (PC -> bb_id hash, per-slice flush, sparse
  rows matching the SimPoint 3.2 sample.bb convention). Plugin args
  `bbv_out=PATH,slice=N` register a per-insn callback that ticks the
  emitter; it is registered BEFORE the icount callback so when both
  fire on the same insn (icount target == slice multiple) the slice
  row is durable before exit(200). The shipped SimPoint binary
  (F12) parses the emitted file without error. Verified end-to-end:
  on icount_spin with ICOUNT=1M,SLICE=10k, SimPoint identifies 2
  phases (startup weight 0.01, steady-state loop weight 0.99) which
  matches the workload's structure.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: BBV emission as a second sub-mode of `hybrid_handoff`
  (not a separate plugin - keeps per-insn callback cost to one
  per insn). New plugin args `bbv_out=PATH,slice=N`. Emit one BBV row
  per `slice` dynamic insns into a SimPoint-readable `.bb` file.
- Key files:
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`
  - `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.c` (new sub-module)
